title: Velocity and position graphs
target: Connect a position-time graph to velocity using slope.
criteria: Read positions and elapsed times from a graph.
Find velocity from position change divided by time.
Explain the difference between speed and velocity.

authoring.limitations: Reasoning evidence only. Multiple choice does not certify physical performance. Teacher reviews before assigning and rates mastery separately.

cpa.prompt: A straight position-time segment runs from (2 s, 7 m) to (6 s, 19 m). What are elapsed time and position change?
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: A position-time graph is horizontal at x = 11 m throughout the interval from 1 to 5 s. What does this show?
options: It is necessarily at the origin.
The object remains at 11 m throughout that interval.
cpa.guide: A continuously horizontal position graph shows no position change.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

cpa.prompt: Take right as positive. A cart moves steadily from 16 m to 4 m in 3 s. What is velocity?
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: A robot is at −2 m at t = 1 s and +13 m at t = 6 s. What is average velocity over that interval?
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: A runner travels 8 m east then 8 m west in 4 s. What are average speed and average velocity?
cpa.guide: Distance = 16 m; displacement = 0. Divide each by 4 s.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: Two carts have equal average velocities over 10 s. Must their average speeds be equal?
options: No; average velocity cannot be measured.
Yes; equal displacement guarantees equal path length.
Yes; speed and velocity are identical.
No; one may travel farther while reversing direction.
cpa.guide: Equal displacement/time does not require equal distance/time.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Select a claim supported by the stated evidence and assumptions.
